compliance.zoning_notes: B2B SaaS company — no physical restaurant. General office zoning applies. If operating from co-working space, ensure sub-lease permits.
licensing_requirements: Data privacy compliance (Texas Business & Commerce Code)
compliance.compliance_timeline: Business registration: 1-2 weeks. Sales tax permit: 2-3 weeks. All achievable in <30 days.
compliance.estimated_costs: Business license: $75-200. Sales tax permit: Free. Standard registration: $300 filing fee.

strategy_bullets: Austin has 3-4 direct competitors — differentiation on workflow automation for mid-size chains is the gap
Partner with Square and Toast rather than compete — integration-first strategy
Target East Austin and SoCo independent restaurants as early adopters; they're tech-savvy and growth-oriented
Leverage Capital Factory network for warm introductions to restaurant tech founders
Texas Restaurant Show in July 2026 is the best launchpad — get a booth or sponsor
recommended_first_week: Register business with Texas Secretary of State and City of Austin
Apply for Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit
Join Austin Technology Council and attend next networking event
Schedule intro meetings with Capital Factory and Austin Chamber of Commerce
Visit SoCo and East Austin restaurant clusters for in-person market research
Secure SXSW 2027 early-bird badge for restaurant tech track

deep_analysis.risk_assessment: Medium risk — 3 established competitors (Toast, Restaurant365, MarginEdge) have Austin presence. However, none specifically target mid-size chain workflow automation end-to-end. The gap exists but requires strong differentiation. Austin restaurant market is growing rapidly, creating a rising tide.
anomalies: Toast POS is listed as competitor but could also be a powerful integration partner — consider partnership-first approach
No restaurant-specific regulation burden (SaaS only) — this is a compliance advantage over physical restaurant businesses
Capital Factory has restaurant tech portfolio companies that could be both competitors and collaborators
recommendations: Launch with a 'Toast integration-first' go-to-market to differentiate from Restaurant365
Pilot with 3-5 SoCo independent restaurants before targeting chains
Hire a local Austin BD rep within first 60 days — Austin values local presence
Use Texas Restaurant Show booth as official market entry announcement
